modal_instances.sentence: I noted then that, "if the outlook changes materially, policy will change as well.
Both the economy and our policy evolved dramatically in ways no one could have predicted.
These two back-to-back world historical crises have left behind scars that will be with us for a long time.
These policies are still emerging, and their longer-term implications will take some time to be seen.

Tariff increases will likely take some time to work their way through supply chains.
As a result, this one-time increase in the price level will likely be spread over several quarters and show up as somewhat higher inflation during that period.
We will carefully assess and manage the risk of higher and more persistent inflation.
We will make sure that this one-time increase in prices does not become an ongoing inflation problem.
If we ease too aggressively, we could leave the inflation job unfinished and need to reverse course later to fully restore 2 percent inflation.
If we maintain restrictive policy too long, the labor market could soften unnecessarily.
We will continue to determine the appropriate stance based on the incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.
